newsitem.title: USA: US spot jet slips on NYMEX, traders sort out diffs.
newsitem.headline: US spot jet slips on NYMEX, traders sort out diffs.

text.p: U.S. spot jet fuel traders Monday said few deals were done because the market was attempting to fix new differential values as prices began being pegged against March futures prices.
Absolute prices fell, however, as March NYMEX heating oil values settled 0.88 cent lower to 65.28 cents a gallon.

Gulf Coast back-fourth cycle 54-grade jet was sold for 1.5 cents over March futures, a touch weaker than Friday diffs. Sixth cycle material was bid at 0.75 cent over, traders said, restrained by concerns over a possible strike by American Airlines workers later this month.
"People are hesitant to do anything in the sixth cycle because they're reluctant to be exposed if there's a strike. They're afraid to get out in front of something like that," one Gulf player said.
American Airlines pilots picketed airports across the United States last week, warning that a lengthy strike at the nation's second-biggest airline could begin Feb. 15.

Union members earlier last month rejected a tentative labor contract that would have given them a five percent pay raise over five years. They are now demanding more than 11 percent and improved stock options and better job security.
New York Harbor 54-grade was talked Monday between 7.0 and 8.0 cents over the March print, but saw little real action.
Some East Coast players said uncertainty about the American Airlines strike and expected arrivals of sizeable shipments next week were keeping a lid on differential values.
((- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1632))
